title: Count Subarrays Where Max Element Appears at Least K Times
summary: Given an integer array and a positive integer k, count the subarrays where the maximum element appears at least k times.
statement: Given an integer array and a positive integer k, count the subarrays where the maximum element appears at least k times. A subarray consists of consecutive elements from the original array.
constraints: nums is nonempty and k is positive.
Use the maximum value of the entire array, not each subarray local maximum.
Count contiguous subarrays containing that value at least k times.
hints: After shrinking past the earliest necessary maximum, every start before left forms a valid subarray ending here.
Track maximum occurrences and advance left while the window has at least k, then add left.
For each right value update count; while count>=k remove nums[left] and advance; accumulate left.
The loop leaves exactly the first invalid start at left, so starts zero through left-1—and only those—retain at least k maxima.
editorial: The loop leaves exactly the first invalid start at left, so starts zero through left-1—and only those—retain at least k maxima.

tests.explanation: Exactly six subarrays include at least two occurrences of the global maximum three.
The global maximum four occurs only once, so no subarray reaches three occurrences.
